subject: Dedicated fleet options & ramp paths — HortonBio opportunity
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@hortonbio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated fleet options & ramp paths — HortonBio opportunity

Oliver — thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together three differentiated dedicated reservation options that align with the forecasted traffic you shared (avg gen load + nightly batch embeddings). Attached is a short packet; summary below. Please review and indicate which path you want us to model into the commercial term sheet.

Option A — Conservative Pilot (30 GPU baseline)
- Cluster: 4 x 8-GPU nodes (NVIDIA A800-equivalent), single AZ
- Minimum guaranteed: 30 GPUs (soft floor)
- Ramp: Week 1 warm-start 30 GPUs, scale to 50 GPUs by end of month 2 if throughput matches forecast
- Use case: tight budget, validate quality/latency on subset of traffic
- Operational: standard monitoring, 7-day SLA for warm-start requests
- Estimated monthly commitment cost: $xxk (see attachment)

Option B — Production Baseline (80 GPU committed)
- Cluster: 10 x 8-GPU nodes across 2 AZs
- Minimum guaranteed: 64 GPUs (hard floor) with burst pool up to 96 GPUs
- Ramp: start at 64 GPUs, scheduled step-up to 80 GPUs at week 6, full 96 burst available on demand (subject to short-term availability)
- Use case: steady production traffic with predictable latency targets
- Operational: A/B rollout windows, canary model pathing, 99.9% availability SLA on committed throughput
- Estimated monthly commitment cost: $yyk

Option C — Anchored Throughput (200 GPU anchored slate)
- Cluster: 25 x 8-GPU nodes across 3 AZs with hot-standby lanes
- Minimum guaranteed: 160 GPUs anchored with 40-GPU burst buffer
- Ramp: negotiated 12-month staircase; 25% activation every quarter until fully active. Includes warm-start credits and pre-warmed KV caches for first 2 months
- Use case: enterprise scale, multi-model inference, strict latency SLAs across regions
- Operational: prioritized routing, dedicated capacity tuning, quarterly review cadence
- Estimated monthly commitment cost: $zzk (discounted for annual commit)

Technical notes: We recommend Option B for latency-sensitive production and Option A to validate model fidelity against your internal eval sets. Option C is best if you prefer an anchored long-term price with prioritized capacity. See the attached spreadsheet for per-token unit economics, example burst scenarios, and model mapping (which model family sits where).

Request: Can you confirm which option you want modeled into the paperwork? Also confirm the preferred ramp aggressiveness (fast: 4 weeks to target vs. gradual: quarter-step) and whether Horton Bio requires on-prem telemetry ingestion (private deployment) for audit reasons.

Attachments: 20260714_dedicated_options_breakdown.pdf, gpu_runbook_estimates.xlsx

— Tessa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0123
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@hortonbio.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Horton Bio Procurement <procurement@hortonbio.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T10:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet options & ramp paths — HortonBio opportunity

Tessa — thanks for the crisp breakdown. A couple quick clarifying questions before we pick a path: 

1) SLA and overage behavior: for Option B, if we need sustained burst >96 GPUs for more than 48 hours due to a large reindex, how do overages get handled? Any soft credits?

2) Region breakout: most of our traffic will be US-east with a small EU footprint for research. For Option C, does multi-AZ mean multi-region routing is supported or would we need a separate footprint in eu-west?

3) Security: Horton requires that inference logs for PHI-like metadata be routed to our tenant KMS and retained for 90 days. Can the private deployment option support the KMS integration while still using Redwood Dedicated for compute?

We like the look of Option B as a starting point but inclined to ask if a shorter ramp (fast: 4 weeks) is possible if you can guarantee a warm-start window for models at activation. Procurement copied here for timing and PO cadence — we’ll need a sample SOW and billing cadence.

Thanks,
Oliver
Head of AI Platform — Horton Bio
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@hortonbio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet options & ramp paths — HortonBio opportunity

Oliver — quick technical clarifications to answer your items: 

- Overage handling: for sustained burst beyond burst pool we propose a grace buffer of 72 hours paid at burst rate, after which sustained overage moves to negotiated ad-hoc capacity pricing. For multi-day heavy reindex we recommend pre-booking an elevated burst window (we can set this in the SOW as a scheduled ramp) which avoids emergency re-provisioning.

- Region breakout: Option C as written is multi-AZ within a single cloud region (us-east). If you need low-latency traffic from eu-west we recommend a small mirror footprint there (recommended 8–16 GPUs) to keep cross-region RTTs low; we can include geo-burst routing so primary compute remains in us-east but sensitive calls route locally.

- KMS / Private telemetry: yes — we support tenant KMS encryption for logs + on-demand private control plane. Compute can remain in Redwood Dedicated while telemetry (logs/traces) routes to your VPC collector and KMS. There are two practical integration patterns: 1) Private Control Plane + Dedicated compute (preferred), or 2) Full Private deployment for on-prem constraints. I suggest pattern (1) for faster time-to-value.

Operational ask: to enable a 4-week fast ramp we need a pre-activation checklist completed (image build, model weights staged to object storage, runbook acceptance). I’ll attach a short pre-activation checklist to the SOW draft.

— Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@hortonbio.com>, Horton Bio Procurement <procurement@hortonbio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-17T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet options & ramp paths — HortonBio opportunity

Oliver / Procurement — thanks for the quick turnaround and the questions — good points. Based on internal alignment with Karthik and Marissa we recommend: 

- Move forward with Option B (Production Baseline) in a fast ramp configuration.
- Ramp profile: start at 64 GPUs (week 0), expand to 80 GPUs at day 21, target full baseline (96 available via burst) by day 30. We will schedule a formal elevated-burst window for any planned reindex events (you can book these at least 14 days in advance).
- SLA / overage: include a 72-hour grace buffer at burst rate for unscheduled spikes; sustained >72 hours will be handled as previously described. We’ll include optional credits in year-1 for up to two scheduled elevated burst windows as goodwill to help with initial onboarding.
- Security / KMS: we’ll provision Private Control Plane + Dedicated compute and wire log export to your tenant KMS with 90-day retention. Karthik will own the integration runbook.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Draft SOW with chosen Option B fast ramp profile, pre-activation checklist, and PO/billing cadence.
2) Draft SSO/KMS integration plan with Karthik and share for Horton security review.
3) Tentatively reserve the 64->80 ramp window starting Aug 3 (subject to PO).

Procurement — can you confirm target PO date and whether you prefer monthly invoicing vs. net-30 consolidated quarterly? Oliver — if you confirm the above by EOD Tuesday I’ll push SOW and a sample invoice for legal/procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Horton live.

— Tessa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
